title: Semidirect discrete logarithm

problem.name: Semidirect discrete logarithm
problem.statement_latex: Given a finite group $G$, an efficiently computable automorphism $\phi$, and $g,h\in G$, find $a$ such that $(g,\phi)^a=(h,\phi^a)$ in $G\rtimes\langle\phi\rangle$. The theorem covers the solvable and matrix-group families specified by Imran--Ivanyos.
problem.statement_text: Given a finite group $G$, an efficiently computable automorphism $\phi$, and $g,h\in G$, find $a$ such that $(g,\phi)^a=(h,\phi^a)$ in $G\rtimes\langle\phi\rangle$. The theorem covers the solvable and matrix-group families specified by Imran–Ivanyos.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|G|)$ quantum time for the covered platform families, through reductions to group-action orbit and discrete-logarithm problems.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|G|)$ quantum time for the covered platform families, through reductions to group-action orbit and discrete-logarithm problems.

classical.headline_latex: $O(\sqrt r)$ group-action operations and storage by semidirect baby-step--giant-step, where $r$ is the orbit period; platform-specific reductions to ordinary discrete logarithms can be faster.
